note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following stable but high-grade biopsy findings and rising PSA.

This 72-year-old ICT consultant, married and living with his partner, presents for urological re-evaluation. His medical history is notable for chronic kidney disease with an eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2 and anaemia (haemoglobin 12.3 g/dL). He is a current smoker with a 38 pack-year history and abstains from alcohol. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 6/35. He maintains a daily walking routine of 20 minutes and recently completed six sessions of physiotherapy for lower back discomfort. His daughter manages communication and is copied on correspondence with his consent. He has no known drug allergies and takes no active medications.

On DRE, the prostate feels normal with no palpable nodules or asymmetry, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination is unremarkable with stable vital signs (BP 127/72 mmHg, HR 74 bpm) and no signs of systemic compromise.
